messages:
maria: heads up — customer traffic to /v1/generate is getting 502s from the gateway policy matcher. looks like the new precedence rule we rolled earlier is mis-ordering the route and hitting the global ratelimit path.
ankur: on it. can you post the matcher snippet? i want to see the conditions.
maria: here's the rule we shipped in prod a few mins ago: ```yaml - name: apply-global-ratelimit match: path_prefix: /v1 actions: - rate_limit: global-tier``` this was supposed to be lower priority than product-specific routes but seems to be taking precedence.
lucas: this rings bell — matcher comparator bug where longer-prefix rules weren't prioritized if `priority` wasn't set explicitly. we saw this in canary but thought the default comparator change had fixed it.
maria: impact: ~20% 502 across EU regions. customers hitting streaming endpoints. we need an emergency unblock that doesn't require a full deploy.
ankur: plan: add a higher-priority temporary override route that matches the streaming prefix and sets a header to opt the requests out of the global ratelimit path. then we can rollback the override after a safety deploy.
maria: exact change?
ankur: patch the gateway config via the admin toggle UI or api: ```json {"action":"upsert_route","route": {"match":{"path_prefix":"/v1/stream","priority":1000},"actions":[{"set_header":{"name":"x-routing-override","value":"no-global-rate"}}]}}``` this route will be evaluated before the global ratelimit because of explicit priority.
lucas: alternative: set `x-rewrite-path` but header opt-out is safer for telemetry and doesn't require rewriting internals.
maria: can we push this via the console toggle? i can do it if we confirm the exact payload.
ankur: yes — use admin console -> Feature Flags -> Routing Overrides -> New override. TTL 30m, scope: prod:eu. apply and monitor.
sre-oncall-bot: NOTE: creating emergency override will trigger audit log and a pager if 5xxs persist after 2 minutes.
maria: creating override now. copying payload to audit: ```{"scope":"prod:eu","route":"/v1/stream","priority":1000,"set_header":{"x-routing-override":"no-global-rate"},"ttl":"30m","created_by":"maria"}```
ankur: confirmed applied in EU cluster-3. please hit with smoke checks.
maria: smoke: curl -v https://api.eu.redwood.com/v1/stream -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" --silent | head -n 5 => 200. latency normal. :thumbsup:
lucas: good. add a short-lived metric filter on gateway to count hits routed to override route: `gateway.route_override.count{route:/v1/stream,region:eu}`. watch for anomalous spike.
maria: filter added. graph looks stable, 502s dropped to ~1%.
ankur: follow-ups: 1) schedule a small patch to ensure matcher comparator treats longer prefixes as higher priority (nullable priority fallback) 2) add an automated safety rollback if override TTL expires and 5xxs reappear 3) cleanup: remove override after full fix is deployed.
lucas: on (1) — i'll open a PR to the matcher lib and link unit tests. 2) devex: can we add a console action to escalate to a routed fallback model instead of opt-out header? product asked for a button.
maria: noted. for now i'm going to annotate the incident and mark as "mitigated".
sre-oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied by maria at 2154322012, 502 rate decreased. continue monitoring.
runtime-bot: deploy 21543.2 to matcher-service succeeded in canary. will promote once PR merged.
maria: ok leaving the override in place for 2 hours while matcher patch rolls. will remove after we confirm the canary. thanks everyone.
ankur: thumbs up — good quick-unblock. please add a postmortem note with timeline and the audit payload.
lucas: will add tests to prevent regressions.
maria: end.
